metadata.title: Fast Exact Matrix Completion: A Unified Optimization Framework for Matrix Completion
metadata.authors: Dimitris Bertsimas and Michael Lingzhi Li

nodes.name: Classical Low-Rank Matrix Completion
nodes.statement: Recover $\bm{X}=\bm{U}\bm{V}^T$ of rank $k$ minimizing $\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(X_{ij}-A_{ij})^2$ subject to $\rank(\bm{X})=k$, given partially observed $\bm{A}\in\md{R}^{n\times m}$ with index set $\Omega$ of known entries.
nodes.statement_clean: Recover a rank-k matrix that fits known entries of A.

nodes.name: Matrix Completion with Side Information and Tikhonov Regularization
nodes.statement: $\min_{\|\bm{S}\|_2=1}\min_{\bm{U}}\frac{1}{nm}\left(\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(X_{ij}-A_{ij})^2+\frac{1}{\gamma}\|\bm{U}\|_2^2\right)$ s.t. $\bm{X}=\bm{U}\bm{S}^T\bm{B}^T$, where $\bm{B}\in\md{R}^{m\times p}$ is the feature matrix.
nodes.statement_clean: Regularized matrix completion that factorizes X using side-information features B.

nodes.name: Diagonal Mask Matrix $\bm{W}_i$
nodes.statement: $\bm{W}_i\in\md{R}^{m\times m}$ is diagonal with $(\bm{W}_i)_{jj}=1$ if $(i,j)\in\Omega$ and $0$ otherwise; $\overline{\bm{a}}_i=\bm{a}_i\bm{W}_i$ is row $i$ of $\bm{A}$ with unknown entries set to $0$.

nodes.name: Reformulated Variable $\bm{V}=\bm{B}\bm{S}$
nodes.statement: Auxiliary matrix $\bm{V}=\bm{B}\bm{S}\in\md{R}^{m\times k}$ used to simplify the separable form of the objective.

nodes.name: $(\alpha,p)$-submatrix full rank
nodes.statement: A matrix $\bm{S}\in\md{R}^{m\times k}$ ($m>k$) is $(\alpha,p)$-submatrix full rank if every $p\times k$ submatrix of $\bm{S}$ has full column rank with minimum singular value at least $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Strict Saddle Function
nodes.statement: $f:\md{R}^d\to\md{R}$ is $(\theta,\zeta,\eta)$-strict saddle if for every $\bm{x}$, at least one of: (1) $\|\nabla f(\bm{x})\|\geq\theta$; (2) $\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(\bm{x}))\leq-\zeta$; (3) $\bm{x}$ is within $\eta$ of a local minimum.
nodes.origin_citation: Ge, Huang, Jin, Yuan 2015 (escaping saddle points)

nodes.name: Row-Sampling Model
nodes.statement: For each row $\bm{a}_i$ of $\bm{A}$, sample $l$ of $m$ entries uniformly without replacement to be observed; effective per-entry probability $r=l/m$.

nodes.name: Projection Matrices $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}}$ and $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}$
nodes.statement: $\bm{S}_i=\bm{W}_i\bm{S}$, $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}}=\bm{I}_m-\bm{S}(\bm{S}^T\bm{S})^{-1}\bm{S}^T$, $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}=\bm{W}_i-\bm{S}_i(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i)^{-1}\bm{S}_i^T$, satisfying $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}}\bm{S}=\bm{0}$ and $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}\bm{S}_i=\bm{0}$.

nodes.name: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error)
nodes.statement: $\text{MAPE}=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{|\hat{A}_{ij}-A_{ij}|}{|A_{ij}|}$, the evaluation metric for matrix recovery accuracy.

nodes.name: Assumption 1: Spread-Out Decomposition
nodes.statement: $\bm{A}=\bm{U}^*\bm{S}^{*T}$ has rank $k$ with $\bm{U}^*\in\md{R}^{n\times k}$, $\bm{S}^*\in\md{R}^{m\times k}$, $\|\bm{S}^*\|=1$, and both $\bm{U}^*,\bm{S}^*$ are $(\alpha,l)$-submatrix full rank with $\alpha>0$.

nodes.name: Assumption 2: Domain Restriction on $\bm{S}$
nodes.statement: The variable $\bm{S}$ is restricted to matrices that are $(\alpha,l)$-submatrix full rank, ensuring $(\bm{S}^T\bm{W}_i\bm{S})^{-1}$ is well-defined wherever $c(\bm{S})$ is evaluated.

nodes.name: Separable Reformulation of Matrix Completion
nodes.statement: Problem (\ref{mainproblem}) is equivalent to $\min_{\|\bm{S}\|_2=1} c(\bm{S})=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{\bm{a}}_i\left(\bm{I}_m-\bm{V}\left(\frac{\bm{I}_k}{\gamma}+\bm{V}^T\bm{W}_i\bm{V}\right)^{-1}\bm{V}^T\right)\overline{\bm{a}}_i^T$ with $\bm{V}=\bm{B}\bm{S}$.
assumptions: $\bm{B}\in\md{R}^{m\times p}$ is the side-information feature matrix
conclusions: The two-level minimization over $(\bm{U},\bm{S})$ collapses to a single minimization over $\bm{S}$ with closed-form inner solution

nodes.name: Matrix Inversion Lemma (Woodbury)
nodes.statement: For $\bm{U}\in\md{R}^{n\times k}$ and $\bm{V}\in\md{R}^{k\times n}$: $(\bm{I}_n+\bm{U}\bm{V})^{-1}=\bm{I}_n-\bm{U}(\bm{I}_k+\bm{V}\bm{U})^{-1}\bm{V}$.

nodes.name: Gradient of $c(\bm{S})$
nodes.statement: $\nabla c(\bm{S})=-\frac{2\gamma}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\bm{B}^T\bm{\gamma}_i(\bm{S})\bm{\gamma}_i(\bm{S})^T\bm{V}$, where $\bm{\gamma}_i(\bm{S})=\left(\bm{I}_m-\bm{V}(\frac{\bm{I}_k}{\gamma}+\bm{V}^T\bm{W}_i\bm{V})^{-1}\bm{V}^T\right)\overline{\bm{a}}_i^T$.
conclusions: Closed-form expression for $\nabla c(\bm{S})$ used in gradient descent

nodes.name: projImpute
nodes.statement: Full projected gradient descent with Nesterov acceleration on the hypersphere $\|\bm{S}\|_2=1$ to minimize $c(\bm{S})$, followed by closed-form recovery of $\bm{A}$.

nodes.name: Random initialization
nodes.statement: $\bm{S}_1\gets$ random matrix with $\|\bm{S}_1\|_2=1$; $\eta_0\gets\infty$; compute initial $\eta_1,\bm{G}_1=c(\bm{S}_1),\nabla c(\bm{S}_1)$; $\nabla\tilde{\bm{S}}_1\gets\bm{0}^{p\times k}$.

nodes.name: Nesterov-accelerated projected gradient loop
Final matrix recovery
nodes.statement: Set $\bm{S}^*\gets\bm{S}_t$; for $i=1,\ldots,n$: $\bm{a}_i\gets\overline{\bm{a}}_i\bm{B}\bm{S}^*(\bm{B}\bm{S}^*\bm{W}_i\bm{B}\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{B}^T)^{-1}\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{B}^T$; return $\bm{A}$.

nodes.name: Computational Complexity of projImpute Steps
nodes.statement: The cost-and-gradient step has complexity $O\left(|\Omega|(p+k^2+\frac{pk+k^3}{m\alpha})\right)$; the final matrix-fill step has complexity $O\left(|\Omega|(k^2+\frac{k}{\alpha}+\frac{k^3}{m\alpha})\right)$, where $\alpha=|\Omega|/(mn)$.
conclusions: Step \ref{calc_cost} complexity: $O(|\Omega|(p+k^2+(pk+k^3)/(m\alpha)))$
Step \ref{calc_final} complexity: $O(|\Omega|(k^2+k/\alpha+k^3/(m\alpha)))$

nodes.name: projImpute Termination and Total Complexity
nodes.statement: projImpute terminates in $t_{max}$ steps with overall complexity $O\left(|\Omega|(p+k^2+\frac{pk+k^3}{m\alpha})\right)$.
conclusions: Total complexity per run is bounded as stated

nodes.name: fastImpute
nodes.statement: Adaptive stochastic projected gradient descent variant of projImpute that subsamples $n_0$ rows and $m_0$ columns per row at each iteration to estimate the gradient.

nodes.name: Sampling-size initialization
nodes.statement: $\alpha\gets|\Omega|/(mn)$; $m_0\gets\min(2p,m)$; $n_0\gets\lfloor\frac{k\sqrt{nm}\log(\sqrt{nm})}{8m_0\alpha}\rfloor$; pick initial $[n_0]\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and per-row $[m_0^i]\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}$; random $\bm{S}_1$ with $\|\bm{S}_1\|_2=1$; compute $\eta_1,\bm{G}_1=c_t(\bm{S}_1),\nabla c_t(\bm{S}_1)$; $\nabla\tilde{\bm{S}}_1\gets\bm{0}^{k\times p}$.

nodes.name: Stochastic Nesterov-projected gradient loop
Final matrix fill
nodes.statement: Set $\bm{S}^*\gets\bm{S}_t$; for $i=1,\ldots,n$ compute $\bm{a}_i\gets\overline{\bm{a}}_i\bm{B}\bm{S}^*(\bm{B}\bm{S}^*\bm{W}_i\bm{B}\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{B}^T)^{-1}\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{B}^T$; return $\bm{A}$.

nodes.name: Stochastic Gradient Approximation Bound
nodes.statement: With probability at least $1-\epsilon$, for any $t$ and $\bm{S}$ with $\|\bm{S}\|=1$: $|c_t(\bm{S})-c(\bm{S})|\leq\sqrt{\frac{Ak\log(k/\epsilon)}{n_0}}$ and $\|\nabla c_t(\bm{S})-\nabla c(\bm{S})\|_2\leq\sqrt{\frac{Bk\log(k/\epsilon)}{n_0}}$.
conclusions: $|c_t(\bm{S})-c(\bm{S})|\leq\sqrt{Ak\log(k/\epsilon)/n_0}$ w.p. $\geq1-\epsilon$
$\|\nabla c_t(\bm{S})-\nabla c(\bm{S})\|_2\leq\sqrt{Bk\log(k/\epsilon)/n_0}$ w.p. $\geq1-\epsilon$
nodes.origin_citation: Adapted from Bertsimas & Li 2018 (interpretable matrix completion)

nodes.name: Strict-Saddle SGD Convergence
assumptions: Noise bound on stochastic gradient as stated
conclusions: SGD with added Gaussian perturbation reaches a $\delta$-neighborhood of a local minimum in $O(\poly(1/\delta))$ iterations
nodes.origin_citation: Fang, Lin, Zhang 2019; Daneshmand et al. 2018; Ge et al. 2015

nodes.name: Gradient Orthogonality at $1/\gamma=0$
nodes.statement: When $1/\gamma=0$, for all $\bm{S}$ and any sample $[n_t],[m_t]$: $\bm{S}^T\nabla c_t(\bm{S})=0$.
conclusions: $\bm{S}^T\nabla c_t(\bm{S})=0$, so the tangent-plane projection step is trivial

nodes.name: Strict-Saddle Property and No-Spurious-Minima of $c(\bm{S})$
nodes.statement: Under row sampling with $r=l/m>Ck/m$ (large $C$), Assumptions \ref{ass:ripweak}-\ref{ass:Vrestrict}, $1/\gamma=0$, $\bm{B}=\bm{I}_m$: w.p. $1-O(1/n)$, $c(\bm{S})$ is $(\epsilon,O(\epsilon/k),O(\sqrt{\epsilon}))$-strict saddle for sufficiently small $\epsilon$, and all local minima are global.
conclusions: $c(\bm{S})$ is $(\epsilon,O(\epsilon/k),O(\sqrt{\epsilon}))$-strict saddle w.p. $1-O(1/n)$
All local minima of $c(\bm{S})$ are global minima

nodes.name: Proof of Strict Saddle and No Spurious Minima
nodes.statement: Show that whenever $\|\nabla c(\bm{S})\|\leq\epsilon$ and $\bm{S}$ is $\eta$-far from a global min, $\nabla^2 c(\bm{S})$ has a negative eigenvalue, by constructing $\bm{M}=\bm{z}^T\bm{x}$ that makes the quadratic form negative.

nodes.name: Reduction to single negative-eigenvalue claim
nodes.statement: It suffices to show: for all $\bm{S}$ with $\|\nabla c(\bm{S})\|\leq\epsilon$ and $\bm{S}$ more than $\eta$-away from any global minimum, $\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 c(\bm{S}))\leq-\zeta$ for some $\zeta>0$. This implies both strict saddle and no-spurious-minima.

nodes.name: Hessian decomposition into four terms
nodes.statement: Decompose $\bm{M}:\nabla^2c(\bm{S}):\bm{M}=\frac{2}{nm}\sum_i(T1+T2-T3+T4)$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:second_deriv}.

nodes.name: Bound terms T2 and T4 via first-derivative condition
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:term_24_bound}, w.p. $\geq1-O(1/n)$ both T2 and T4 sums are $\leq Kr\epsilon\|\bm{M}\|^2$ for absolute constants.

nodes.name: Construct $\bm{M}=\bm{z}^T\bm{x}$
nodes.statement: Set $\bm{z}^T$ as a non-zero rescaled column of $\bm{P}_{\bm{S}}\bm{S}^*$ and $\bm{x}^T$ as the small eigenvector from Lemma \ref{lem:eigvec_existence}, with $\|\bm{M}\|=1$.

nodes.name: Bound T1 (small) and T3 (large positive)
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:term_1_bound}, $T1=O(r\epsilon)$. By Lemma \ref{lem:term_3_bound}, $T3\geq O(r\eta^2/k)$.

nodes.name: Combine to negative quadratic form
nodes.statement: $\bm{M}:\nabla^2c(\bm{S}):\bm{M}\leq O(r\epsilon)+O(r\epsilon)-O(r\eta^2/k)+O(r\epsilon)=-O(r\eta^2/k)$ when $\epsilon\leq O(\eta^2/k)$, giving $\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 c(\bm{S}))\leq-O(r\epsilon/k)$ for $\eta=O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$.

nodes.name: First Derivative of $c(\bm{S})$ (Appendix form)
nodes.statement: $\nabla c(\bm{S})=\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}\bm{a}_i^T\bm{a}_i\bm{S}_i(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i)^{-1}$. Each summand is orthogonal to $\bm{S}$ since $\bm{S}^T\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}=\bm{0}$.
conclusions: Closed-form derivative; orthogonality to $\bm{S}$

nodes.name: Hessian Quadratic Form of $c(\bm{S})$
nodes.statement: For $\bm{M}\in\md{R}^{m\times k}$: $\bm{M}:\nabla^2 c(\bm{S}):\bm{M}=\frac{2}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n(T_1+T_2-T_3+T_4)$, where the four terms are explicit quadratic-rational expressions in $\bm{a}_i,\bm{S}_i,\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i},\bm{M}$.
conclusions: Explicit Hessian-direction formula used to analyze the saddle structure

nodes.name: Bound on Hessian Terms T2 and T4
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:ripweak}-\ref{ass:Vrestrict}, $\|\nabla c(\bm{S})\|\leq\epsilon$, $r>Ck/m$ (large $C$): w.p. $\geq1-O(1/n)$, the T2 and T4 sums are bounded by $Kr\epsilon\|\bm{M}\|^2$ and $Lr\epsilon\|\bm{M}\|^2$ for absolute constants $K,L$.
conclusions: T2 sum norm $\leq Kr\epsilon\|\bm{M}\|^2$ w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$
T4 sum norm $\leq Lr\epsilon\|\bm{M}\|^2$ w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$

nodes.name: Existence of Small-Eigenvalue Eigenvector
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:ripweak}-\ref{ass:Vrestrict}, $\|\nabla c(\bm{S})\|\leq\epsilon$ small, and $\min_{\bm{R}^T\bm{R}=\bm{I}}\|\bm{S}-\bm{S}^*\bm{R}\|\geq\eta$: $\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{S}(\bm{S}^T\bm{S})^{-1}$ has an eigenvector with eigenvalue of size $O(\epsilon)$.
conclusions: $\bm{S}^{*T}\bm{S}(\bm{S}^T\bm{S})^{-1}$ has eigenvalue of magnitude $O(\epsilon)$

nodes.name: Bound on Hessian Term T1
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses and with $\bm{M}=\bm{z}^T\bm{x}$ as constructed: w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$, $\left\|\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n\bm{a}_i\bm{S}_i(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i)^{-1}\bm{M}^T\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}\bm{M}(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i)^{-1}\bm{S}_i^T\bm{a}_i^T\right\|\leq O(r\epsilon)$.
conclusions: T1 norm $\leq O(r\epsilon)$ w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$

nodes.name: Lower Bound on Hessian Term T3
nodes.statement: Under the same hypotheses and with $\bm{M}=\bm{z}^T\bm{x}$: w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$, $\frac{1}{nm}\sum_{i=1}^n\bm{a}_i\bm{M}(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i)^{-1}\bm{M}^T\bm{P}_{\bm{S}_i}\bm{a}_i^T\geq O(r\eta^2/k)$.
conclusions: T3 sum $\geq O(r\eta^2/k)$ w.p. $\geq 1-O(1/n)$

nodes.name: General Hoeffding-Type Concentration
nodes.statement: If $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent with $\md{P}(|X_i-a_i|\geq\sigma_i\sqrt{\log(1/\epsilon)})\leq\epsilon$, then $\md{P}\left(\left|\frac{\sum_i(X_i-a_i)}{n}\right|\geq\frac{2\sqrt{\sum_i\sigma_i^2}}{n}\sqrt{\log(1/(4\epsilon))}\right)\leq\epsilon$.
conclusions: Concentration of $\frac{1}{n}\sum(X_i-a_i)$ at the stated rate

nodes.name: Sample-Population Inverse Deviation Bound
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{ass:Vrestrict}: $\md{P}\left(\left\|(\bm{S}^T\bm{S}/m)^{-1}-(\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i/l)^{-1}\right\|\leq\sqrt{D\log(1/\epsilon)/l}\right)\geq1-\epsilon$.
conclusions: Inverse-Gram matrix deviation bound at rate $\sqrt{\log(1/\epsilon)/l}$

nodes.name: Matrix Perturbation Inversion Inequality
nodes.statement: If $\bm{A},\bm{B}=\bm{A}+\bm{\Delta}$ are invertible: $\|\bm{A}^{-1}-\bm{B}^{-1}\|\leq\|\bm{A}^{-1}\|\|\bm{B}^{-1}\|\|\bm{\Delta}\|$.

nodes.name: Sample-Population Gram Matrix Deviation
nodes.statement: $\md{P}\left(\left\|\bm{S}^T\bm{S}/m-\bm{S}_i^T\bm{S}_i/l\right\|\leq\sqrt{C\log(1/\epsilon)/l}\right)\geq1-\epsilon$.
conclusions: Gram-matrix sample-vs-population deviation $\sim\sqrt{\log(1/\epsilon)/l}$

nodes.name: Matrix Chernoff Bound
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{X}\subset\md{R}^{k\times k}$ PSD with $\max\lambda_{\max}(\bm{X})\leq D$, sampling $\ell$ matrices uniformly without replacement: $\md{P}(\lambda_{\min}(\sum_j\bm{X}_j)\leq(1-\delta)\mu_{\min})\leq k\exp(-\delta^2\mu_{\min}/(4D))$ for $\delta\in[0,1)$, and analogously for $\lambda_{\max}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{X}$ finite set of PSD $k\times k$ matrices with bounded $\lambda_{\max}\leq D$
conclusions: Tail bounds on extreme eigenvalues of random PSD sums
nodes.origin_citation: Tropp 2012 (user-friendly tail bounds for matrix sums)

nodes.name: fastImpute Per-Step Complexity (with side info)
nodes.statement: With $m_0=O(p)$ and $n_0=\max\{O(nk\log n/(m_0\alpha)),\underline{n}\}$, the gradient-update step of fastImpute has complexity $O\left(\frac{(pk+k^3)n\log n}{\alpha}\right)$.
conclusions: fastImpute step complexity $O((pk+k^3)n\log n/\alpha)$ — independent of $m$

nodes.name: Global Convergence under Row Sampling
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:ripweak}-\ref{ass:Vrestrict}, $1/\gamma=0$, $\bm{B}=\bm{I}_m$, row-sampling rate $r>Ck/m$ for $C$ large: fastImpute (with perturbation) outputs a point $\delta$-close to a global minimum in $\poly(1/\delta)$ iterations w.p. $1-O(1/n)$.
conclusions: fastImpute reaches $\delta$-neighborhood of global min in $\poly(1/\delta)$ steps w.p. $1-O(1/n)$

nodes.name: Global Convergence under Uniform (Bernoulli) Sampling
nodes.statement: Under the same setting but uniform sampling at rate $r_0>\frac{Cnk\log n}{mn}$: fastImpute outputs a point $\delta$-close to a global minimum in $\poly(1/\delta)$ iterations w.p. $1-O(1/n)$.
conclusions: Same global convergence guarantee under Bernoulli sampling, gaining a $\log n$ factor

nodes.name: fastImpute Step Complexity without Side Information
nodes.statement: For $m=p$ and $\bm{B}=\bm{I}_m$, the gradient-update step of fastImpute has complexity $O\left(\frac{k^3 d\log d}{\alpha}\right)$ where $d=\min\{m,n\}$.
conclusions: Symmetric problem yields $O(k^3 d\log d/\alpha)$ per step

nodes.name: Pathological Sparse Matrix
nodes.statement: $\bm{A}$ with $A_{11}=1$ and all other entries $0$ cannot be recovered from sub-sampled entries unless $A_{11}$ is observed; this motivates Assumption \ref{ass:ripweak} (no element of the decomposition is special).

nodes.name: Synthetic-Data Experiments (with side info)
nodes.statement: Generate $\bm{A}=\bm{U}\bm{S}^T\bm{B}^T$ with uniform $[0,1]$ entries and missing fraction $\mu$; sweep $(m,n,p,k,\mu)$; compare fastImpute vs. projImpute vs. IMC on time and MAPE.

nodes.name: Netflix Real-World Experiment (with side info)
nodes.statement: Five Netflix subsets ranging from $3{,}923\times 103$ (Base) to $471{,}268\times 14{,}538$ (Full), with 59 TMDB features; fastImpute beats IMC on time and MAPE at every scale (e.g. Full: 2934s vs. 7605s, MAPE 20.7\% vs. 21.0\%).

nodes.name: Synthetic-Data Experiments (no side info)
nodes.statement: Sweep $(m,n,k,\mu)$ comparing fastImpute against SIALS, SISVD, MFSGD, GROUSE; on large realistic combinations fastImpute is on average $\sim$10\% of competitors' time and reduces MAPE by 40-70\%.

nodes.name: Netflix Real-World Experiment (no side info)
nodes.statement: Same five Netflix subsets without features; fastImpute beats SIALS at every scale (e.g. Full: 2098s vs. 38256s, MAPE 13.8\% vs. 20.1\%).

nodes.name: IMC (Inductive Matrix Completion)
nodes.statement: Benchmark inductive matrix completion algorithm with regularization parameter $\lambda$ tuned per problem; used as the comparison baseline for fastImpute with side information.

nodes.name: softImpute-ALS (SIALS)
nodes.statement: Alternating least squares matrix completion baseline with spectral regularization, recognized as a state-of-the-art scalable method.

nodes.name: softImpute-SVD (SISVD)
nodes.statement: Original softImpute algorithm using truncated SVDs and spectral regularization.

nodes.name: Matrix Factorization SGD (MFSGD)
nodes.statement: Stochastic gradient descent on the factorization $\bm{A}=\bm{U}\bm{V}$ with separate updates for $\bm{U}$ and $\bm{V}$.

nodes.name: GROUSE
nodes.statement: Online matrix completion via sequential gradient updates on the Grassmann manifold.

nodes.name: Necessity of Regularization
nodes.statement: Tikhonov regularization is needed (a) for robustness when $\bm{A}$ is not exactly low-rank and (b) when row $\bm{a}_i$ has fewer than $k$ known entries so that $\bm{S}^T\bm{W}_i\bm{S}$ is singular.

nodes.name: General Matrix Completion as Special Case
nodes.statement: Setting $p=m$ and $\bm{B}=\bm{I}_m$ in the side-information formulation reduces it to the standard low-rank matrix completion problem with no features.

nodes.name: Row vs. Uniform Sampling Equivalence
nodes.statement: Convergence under row-sampling rate $r$ implies convergence under uniform (Bernoulli) sampling rate $r_0=O(\log n)\,r$, with the $\log n$ factor arising from a coupon-collector argument (Cand\`es, Recht; Gross).
